fatal_errors: Identifies coherent interfaces as producing the mechanism transition, whereas the reported transition occurs in the λ = 16 nm multilayer with semicoherent FCC/BCC interfaces.
Places the phenomenon at 800–1000 °C under high stress, although the target study used room-temperature, 5 mN nanoindentation creep.
Does not identify the Al-Cr-Fe-Ni multilayer, the λ = 16 nm material, or the modulation-period series used to control interface structure.
Attributes the transition only to hindered partial-dislocation motion and omits the proposed pileup, localized stress, interfacial amorphization, and enhanced atomic diffusion/interface slip.
Invents a 30% creep-rate reduction and an incoherent-interface baseline that are not supported by the target results.
The cited evidence concerns a bulk high-entropy superalloy and HEA nanowires, not coherency-controlled FCC/BCC HEA multilayer nanoindentation creep.
explanation: The hypothesis recognizes interface coherency as relevant and broadly invokes impeded dislocation motion, but it reconstructs neither the decisive material nor the observed transition. The appropriate material is the λ = 16 nm Al-Cr-Fe-Ni multilayer with semicoherent interfaces and misfit dislocations. It showed the lowest stress exponents, approximately 1.5–2.6, consistent with diffusion or interface-slip-mediated creep, while the coherent M8 and grain-boundary-dominated M32/M80 samples generally showed dislocation-mediated creep. The proposed high-temperature boundary, quantitative improvement, and baseline are fabricated. Its experiment measures creep rate and coherency but lacks stress-exponent or other measurements needed to discriminate diffusion/interface slip from dislocation creep.
